speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We hope to see more companies create a health promoting working environment for their staff.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There continues to be a debate on e-cigarettes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Any product that contains nicotine can cause addiction and pose risks to health, including e-cigarettes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will allow e-cigarettes only if they are scientifically proven to be effective nicotine replacement therapy products, for smoking cessation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The public consultation will end on 16 March 2018, and we invite interested parties to submit their views.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A final decision on whether to introduce the standardised packaging proposal will be made only after the public consultation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will ensure that any measures, if introduced, are consistent with Singapore’s domestic laws and international obligations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MOH will continue to invest and promote good health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will work closely with individuals, families, industry and community partners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: But personal responsibility for healthy living remains key.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Each of us has to do our part.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our goal is to realise a sustainable healthcare future where all Singaporeans enjoy Better Health, Better Care, Better Life.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: As I understand it, Singaporeans who are training abroad to be doctors, the numbers of them could reach the same number every year.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I am just wondering how the Ministry is looking into these numbers and factoring them into our manpower planning plans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Also, are we still quite dependent on foreign medical manpower to meet our medical needs for the near future?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I am glad to hear about the remuneration framework.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: But as we have just heard from MSF, social service professionals are looking at up to a 12% rise in their remuneration package.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: So, I am just asking whether our nurses can also look forward to such salary increases, to attract more local nurses into the workforce.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor and review their pay to make sure that they remain competitive.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But in addition to that, of course, we also continue to look at their professional development and career progression to make sure that it would be an attractive profession to recruit and to retain nurses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, one of the things we have also done is to have an assistant nurse clinician role added in so that there will be more of them who can get promoted at an earlier stage.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to doctors, yes, indeed, we regularly monitor the demand and supply of doctors, taking into account demographics as well as disease trends.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do offer pre-employment training grants to Singaporeans who are graduates from recognised overseas universities and we will have to take the total number into account, even as we monitor demand and supply.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: The number of persons with dementia is increasing and the Senior Minister of State shared a lot of details on the services and support available for them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: But I would like to know what about their caregivers?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: What are the support and services available for them?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: My second clarification: may I also know what MOH is doing in enhancing palliative care services?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In terms of support for caregivers, over the years, we have implemented quite a lot of support for caregivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For dementia, as I have said earlier in my speech, we are introducing a Dementia Friends mobile app.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is to complement the range of services that we provide to help the caregivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The mobile app is really to help caregivers in terms of providing resources, as well as push notifications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, if their loved ones get lost, Dementia Friends is just like the Singapore Civil Defence Force's (SCDF's) First Responder mobile app.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You can receive push notifications and try to help to find the loved ones.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But there are other services that we provide, the Eldersit Programme, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Eldersitter can actually look after the loved one at home, whilst the caregiver takes her rest or needs to do other work.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have got Weekend Centre-based Respite Care, long-term Nursing Home Respite Care for seven to 30 days and so on; as well as Caregivers Training Grant to help caregivers get training through AIC programmes, for instance, to be better able to care for their loved ones.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, there is a range of services that we provide, including the Singapore Silver Line, Singapore Silver Pages webpage where caregivers can also access resources, services, referrals and information.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For palliative care, we have been expanding the number of in-patient palliative care beds, for instance, as well as home palliative care services, increasing the capacity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have just said that there is the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), where we are now also providing a subsidy through SMF for home palliative care, in terms of consumables.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, my cut on breast cancer has not been answered.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank Dr Lily Neo for her question and let me apologise that I was not able to reply to the cut due to lack of time for my other colleagues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think this is likely due to improvements in treatment, as Dr Lily Neo had alluded to.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards access to breast cancer screening, HPB's Screen for Life currently offers subsidised screening programme at participating polyclinics to women aged 50 and above, and close to 43,300 women have benefited from this programme last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, HPB collaborates with partners like Singapore Cancer Society, as well as Breast Cancer Foundation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These partners provide full sponsorship of screening programmes for lower-income women, such as CHAS cardholders, so that they do not even have to pay $50 to get screening.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This year, to increase the number of women screened, HPB will work with the National Healthcare Group Diagnostics, as well as the community partners and healthcare institutions to bring the Mammobus, the mobile mammogram service, closer to the target population, to 12 additional sites.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All of us, indeed, have a part to play in ensuring that people around us, our loved ones, do go for their mammogram screening.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I would also like to ask that given the prevalence and complications of gestational diabetes, what is the Ministry doing to increase awareness and control the incidence of gestational diabetes amongst women in Singapore.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Have we utilised all means to bring them back into the workforce, especially in the ILTC sector?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: The second clarification is on emplacing graduands, that means, new entrants to nursing.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Is there a difference between a diploma graduand and a degree graduand?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi
text: Can we break the glass ceiling and emplace them correctly since they will be doing the same job?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For the non-practising nurses, in fact, we have enhanced our Return-to-Nursing programme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we have done is to change this into a Place-and-Train programme, so that the nurses who are coming back will be placed first before they go for training, refresher course.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, they will be paid a salary instead of an allowance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the last two years, we have been able to get about 25 non-practising nurses back into practice in the community care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are doing as much as we can to encourage the non-practising nurses to come back into the sector, particularly in the community care sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For new entrants, staff nurses, diploma and graduate nurses, basically, our public healthcare institutions are paying our nurses or healthcare professionals on a performance basis, not just based on qualifications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But for new entrants, that is, people who have very little or no working experience, academic qualifications will be used as a basis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For degree graduates, they have gone through at least six years of post-secondary education.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When they join the profession, they are paid at the Staff Nurse Grade I level, simply because they have gone through a longer period of training and they would have attained deeper skills to kick off, as well as the fact that when they are employed, they would likely be assuming a wider breadth or scope of duties.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For diploma graduates, their post-secondary education is around three years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will be able to start work after that and they would then have the same opportunities as the graduate nurses to progress in their career.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, after they join, both diploma and degree graduates will be assessed based on their performance, as well as any additional specialised skills that they would have gotten in the in-service training.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have a clarification for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Following from hon Member Dr Chia Shi-Lu's point on review of social workers' salaries, because we have a big group of medical social workers in our public healthcare institutions, I hope MOH can consider reviewing this as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I am speaking on behalf of all my sisters and brothers from HSEU.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Is it for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor as well?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question is not for Dr Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am very glad to hear from Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin that we are now only allowed to serve healthier choice drinks in our schools, but I believe these are limited to canned and packet drinks.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One of my friends told me his son became chubbier after going to school because he discovered this thing called "Ice Milo Dinosaur".

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To those of us who are not familiar, "Ice Milo Dinosaur" is ice milo with a heap of raw milo powder.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: So, I hope MOH can work with the schools to eliminate this "abnormality".

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Amrin, you know what is "Ice Milo Dinosaur"?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The current focus is on pre-packaged drinks, but we will certainly look into freshly brewed drinks later on, especially given the Member's concern on ice Milo.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think Senior Minister of State Amy would be relieved that my question is not for her.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Louis Ng for his question.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I apologise for not having enough time to address it earlier during my speech.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The CDMP, in deciding what conditions are covered, we have a CDMP Clinical Advisory Committee which comprises healthcare professionals from the public, as well as the private sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: They will review the various conditions based on considerations, such as the disease's prevalence and the effectiveness of earlier interventions to reduce complications.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, certainly, we will refer the suggestion from Mr Louis Ng to the Advisory Committee for their discussion and review.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This is also picking on the healthier choice point.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Any progress we make towards encouraging people to take healthier choice is good.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But I would like to make two suggestions.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In fact, I understand Milo is considered "healthier choice", but people may be misled into thinking that means it is healthy.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Likewise, many breakfast cereals which have lots of sugar are also labelled as "healthier choice" even though that just means they are healthier than something else, but they are not healthier than, say, bread, even white bread.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, I think it may be good to have absolute standards.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And the second suggestion is: whether we want to take this even further and encourage or require companies to label sugar content in full, given if that is what the main focus is.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Member is right that "healthier choice" symbol does not mean that you can "whack" and "take" as much as you can!

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The key thing is that "healthier choice" is decided based on, for that category of food, it is lower in terms of sugar or other not too healthy things.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is healthier for that food band or for that food category.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: That is something we are working towards and we will update this House, as well as seek public consultations before making a decision on this.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am not sure how "whack" and "take" would appear in the Hansard.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Chia, you want to raise a clarification?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Just one quick clarification for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I talked about the 10% increase in excise duty for tobacco.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: It seems that it has been an ongoing thing.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Could we have an idea of how useful these taxes are, in terms of reducing smoking prevalence?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Some people say that 10% is too little.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: So, perhaps I could have the Parliamentary Secretary's comment on that.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Tobacco taxes complement other measures to reduce smoking.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, price and tax on tobacco have shown to be one of the most effective methods in reducing demand as well as subsequent demand for tobacco products.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There have been numerous studies that have documented that price as well as tax increases have an effect in reducing demand or affecting demand.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Holistically, we have to see that, in toto, our measures have been effective and the Government will continue to review and to see what we can do to enhance this to achieve our vision of a tobacco-free and nicotine-free future.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think we have come to the end of clarification time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would the Member wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: First of all, I would like to thank all Members for their healthy participation in this debate and, of course, as usual, to thank Minister Gan Kim Yong, Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min and Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin and, of course, all the staff of MOH for their detailed clarifications.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I wish them every success in their efforts to transform healthcare for Singaporeans, for now and for the future.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: Thus, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
